full_judgment:
2. The Agrani Bank Ltd. (decree-holder) obtained Rule in WP No. 12231 of 2013 challenging an order bearing No. 12 dated 05-11-2013 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka in Artha Execution Case No. 204 of 2012 arising out of Artha Rin Suit No.8 of 2012 rejecting Bank's application under section 33(2ga) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (the Act, 2003) and thereby accepting the highest bid of respondent No. 2 (auction purchaser) in the auction process held on 31-10-2013. 

 3. The Bank obtained another Rule in writ petition No. 30 of 2014 challenging order No. 17 dated 1-12-2013 of the aforementioned Artha Rin Adalat rejecting the Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 2013 filed under Order XXI Rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code) read with sections 26/57 of the Act, 2003 filed in the aforementioned Artha Execution Case No. 204 of 2012 for setting aside the auction sale. 

 4. The borrower-judgment debtor also obtained Rule in WP No. 89 of 2014 challenging the order No. 17 dated 1-12-2013 passed by the aforesaid Artha Rin Adalat rejecting the Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 2013 filed under Order XXI Rule 90 of the Code read with section 57 of the Act, 2003 for setting aside the auction sale in connection with the aforementioned Artha Rin Execution Case No. 204 of 2012. 

 6. Thereafter, the Bank put the decree in execution through Artha Execution Case No. 204 of 2012 for recovery of Taka 21,29,24,069 with interest till realization. In the execution process the Adalat directed to sell the mortgaged properties under section 33 of the Act, 2003. Accordingly, opening the bid on 31-10-2013 three participants (bidders) were found and first bid was for Taka 10 crore while the second and third bids were for Taka 5(five) crore and Taka 3(three) crore respectively and that although the highest bidder paid the 10% earnest money but the two other bidders did not pay the entire earnest money in accordance with section 33(2) of the Act, 2003. Immediately after opening the bid, considering low price offer, the learned advocate for the decree-holder-Bank filed an application seeking 7(seven) days time to place opinion about auction price after consultation with the Bank but the Adalat rejected the said petition and accepted the bid for Taka 10 crore and fixed on 28-11-2013 for depositing the balance auction money. On 5-11-2013 the Bank again filed an application with an affidavit under section 33(2ga) read with section 57 of the Act, 2003 for setting aside the auction sale alleging insufficient value of auctioned property. But the Adalat rejected the said application by the impugned order dated 5-11-213 (challenged in Writ Petition No. 12231 of 2013). 

 7. Thereafter, the Bank filed Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 2013 on 28-11-2013 under Order XXI Rule 90 of the Code read with sections 26/57 of the Act, 2003 for setting aside the auction sale alleging perpetration of fraud and irregularity in the auction process. The Adalat fixed the date on 1-12-2013 for hearing the miscellaneous case on point of maintain-ability and ultimately by the impugned order dated 1-12-2013 the miscellaneous case was rejected holding it not maintainable (challenged in Writ Petition No. 30 of 2014). 

 8. Borrower judgment-debtor also filed Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 2013 on 17-11-2013 under Order XXI Rule 90 of the Code read with section 57 of the Act, 2003 for setting aside the auction sale alleging commission of fraud and irregularity. The Adalat by the impugned order dated 1-12-2013 rejected the said miscellaneous case as not maintainable (challenged in Writ Petition No. 89 of 2014). 

 9. In this backdrop, challenging the order dated 5-11-2013 rejecting the Bank's application under section 33(2ga) of the Act, 2003 the bank filed WP No. 12231 of 2013 and obtained Rule. At the same time the Bank obtained Rule in WP No. 30 of 2014 challenging the order of the Adalat rejecting the Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 2013 under Order XXI Rule 90 of the Code and the judgment-debtor (borrower) also obtained Rule in WP No. 89 of 2014 challenging the order of the Adalat dated 1-12-2013 rejecting the Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 2013 filed under Order XXI Rule 90 of the Code. 

 14. He also submits that the Bank filed miscellaneous case under Order XXI Rule 90 of the Code alleging that three persons of the same family by making pay orders from the same branch of one bank at the same sitting collusively submitted the bids in order to create impression upon the Adalat about a competitive price and thereby perpetrating fraud upon the Adalat, the auction purchaser obtained the order of acceptance of bid at a shockingly low price. Thus, fraud and irregularity being alleged, the Adalat ought to have made an enquiry in connection with the miscellaneous case. But without doing so, arbitrarily on the date of hearing the Adalat rejected the miscellaneous case outright on point of maintainability. 

 19. Mr Hassan Ariff also contends that although the Adalat fixed the miscellaneous case for hearing on maintainability but on that date the Bank as well as the borrower could not make out any prima-facie case and hence the Adalat assigning cogent reason rejected their miscellaneous cases. As such, there is no illegality in the impugned orders for interference under judicial review of this. Court. He again contends that considering the mouza rate of the concerned area, the Adalat came to the decision as to the price of the mortgaged property and on the other hand, the Bank and the borrower could not show a single scarp of paper as to the higher price of the property in question. Therefore, the sale which has been effected by the Bai-Nama and delivery of possession infavour of the auction purchaser, should not be interfered at this stage. 

 20. We have gone through the writ petitions, the affidavits-in-opposition filed by the auction purchaser in the respective writ petitions, the supplementary-affidavits filed by both the parties, the cited cases and other materials on record. 

 24. In the aforesaid scenario, question arises before us as to whether the Adalat should accept the highest offer inspite of raising objection by the Bank and the borrower by filing application under section 33(2ga) and ultimately by filing miscellaneous cases under Order 21 Rule 90 of the Code. 

 27. But in this particular case, it is the admitted position that the Bank has got the outstanding decretal dues around Taka 21 (twenty) crore against the borrower along with upto date interest and this property is the only security against the liability. At the time of sanctioning loan, the bank assessed consideration value of the property at Taka 20.21 crore and, as such, it rightly raised objection before the Adalat alleging that the bid price was exorbitantly low. The very opening day of bid the Bank's lawyer filed application raising objection to the offer and so on this particular situation the Adalat should consider his application giving an opportunity to the Bank to explain their position relating to the value of property. But instead of doing so, the Adalat hurriedly accepted the bid. 

 28. Under the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, in course of realization of Banks' loan when the property is mortgaged as security, the Adalat disposes the same for the interest of the Bank in order to recover its dues and in doing so the Adalat acts as an handling agent. By the decree under artha rin suit and on failure to pay it by the judgment debtor, the Act, 2003 provides procedure to dispose of mortgaged property by the Adalat under section 33 of the said Act by way of selling the same through auction or by issuing certificate in favour of the decree-holder-Bank under section 33(5) of the said provision whereby the Bank itself can again sell the said property through auction and thirdly, the Bank has got another option to get the property by way of title certificate under section 33(7) of the Act. Therefore, the Adalat is not obliged to sell the property even at the lower price, particularly, when the Bank (decree-holder) raises objection to the value and it has the scope to dispose of the said property under sections 33(5) and or 33(7) of the Act, 2003. But contrary to the said position, here the Adalat was in a hurry to sell the mortgaged property which raises a serious doubt in handling the auction process by the Adalat in this particular case. This view of ours finds support from the case of Agrani Bank Ltd. vs Secretary, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs and others reported in 20 BLC 329 = 19 MLR 330.. Relevant portions of said ratio are as follows:- 

 29. The aforesaid ratio is also accepted in the case of Jubak Housing and Real Estate Development Ltd. vs Judge, Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka and others reported in 23 BLC 186 relevant portions of which are as follows :-"We are in full agreement with the principle of the decision enunciated in the case of Agrani Bank Limited vs The Secretary, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and others reported in 19 MLR 330 = 20 BLC 329 relied upon by Mr Khair Ezaz Maswood that where it is proved that in an auction sale, the offered price is abnormally and shockingly low, in that event, the Artha Rin Adalat is not bound to accept the highest offer particularly when there is an alternative provision for disposing of the judgment-debtors' mort-gaged properties towards satisfaction of the decretal dues in the Ain of 2003." 

 30. In both the aforesaid cases, one of us was a party (JBM Hassan, J). Further in the case of Rupali Bank Ltd. vs Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat and others reported in 17 BLC 217 their Lordships held as under: 

 31. It further appears that the Bank as well as the borrower filed separate miscellaneous cases before the Adalat making specific allegations that although three bids were purportedly shown participated in the auction process but three pay orders of all the offers relating to deposit of earnest money, were prepared from the same branch of a particular bank on a same sitting on a day having the continuous serial numbers i.e. PO No. 3157296, PO No. 3157297 and PO No. 3157298 and that relationship among the three bidders are son, father and his brother. Moreso, from the three bidders although the highest bidder deposited the entire earnest money as per requirement of law, but the two others did not deposit the entire earnest money. For our better under-standing the bit sheet (Annexure-B to the Writ Petition No. 12231 of 2013) is quoted herein below:— 

 33. At the same time, the borrower and the Bank consistently raised objection against the shockingly low offer of the property. On 27-11-2013 the Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 2013 was filed by the Bank. But on the very next working day, [next two days i.e. 28th and 29th November were the Friday and Saturday (weekly holidays)) on 1-12-2013 was the date fixed by the Adalat for hearing the miscellaneous case on maintainability. But on that date the Adalat rejected the said miscellaneous case on merit without making any investigation over the allegations inspite of having two vital issues in the miscellaneous case as to the price of the property as well as the manner of submitting the bids by practising fraud. Thus, outright rejection of miscellaneous case by the Adalat smacks collusion in conducting the auction process inasmuch as the Adalat could accommodate time to the Bank for submitting materials relating to the allegation as brought under the miscellaneous case. But instead of doing so and without making any investigation on the allegation of fraud and shockingly low price, the Adalat hurriedly rejected the said miscellaneous case outright although the date was fixed for hearing on maintainability. Under the aforesaid scenario, we are of the view that in conducting the aforesaid auction process the price of the property is exorbitantly low which is itself a irregularity within the ambit of Order XXI Rule 90 of the Code. This view of ours finds support in the case of XIV (ADC) 465 relevant portions of the said ratio are as follows:- 

 Learned counsel appearing for the auction purchaser and the bank fail to meet the query when their attention was drawn as regards the selling of the tannery at a low price. Learned counsel appearing for the bank submits that the bank has no hand in the process of sale of the property and it is the receiver who has conducted the sale. We want to make it clear that the courts should be cautious in conducting sale of any mortgaged property at a low price and  if it finds that the property is sold at the low price, it should not approve the sale.  Because this court noticed in many cases that even after selling the mortgaged property the debtors remain indebted to the financial institutions if the decretal amount is higher than the sale price. Most of the debtors could not pay the outstanding dues for various reasons. Such default cannot be imputed upon them alone in all cases." 

 34. Secondly, since fraud has been appeared in conducting the auction within a short span of time and by submitting bids, we consider that the total auction process is a nullity and cannot sustain in eye of law. This view of ours, finds support in the case reported in 22 BLC (AD) 139 wherein identical scenario having been found the Apex court held that fraud was perpetrated in conducting auction and consequently, the auction sale was set-aside. Relevant portions of the said decision are quoted herein below:- 

 35. Another aspect as we find that the property is situated under the District Gazipur and on the other hand, the executing court is at Dhaka. It is the consistent view of our High Court Division by several cases, in particular, in the case of Guishana Ara Begum and others vs Judge, Artha Rin Adalat No. 1 Dhaka and another reported in 70 DLR 230, their lordships held that to get the maximum price of the property for the benefit of the decree-holder Bank as well as the borrower, the auction process in an execution proceeding under the Artha Rin Adalat has to be conducted within the jurisdiction of the property concerned. Relevant portions of the said ratio are as follows: 

 "We have already seen that under section 27(1) of the Ain, the Artha Rin Adalat is empowered to transfer an execution case to a different district and the mortgaged property having been situated at Narayanganj, we are of the view that the execution case has been lawfully filed before the Adalat, but the execution case ought to have been transferred to Artha Rin Adalat, Narayanganj for execution of the decree relating to the mortgaged property situated at Narayanganj so that the property is sold at the maximum price. If the mortgaged property is sold at a maximum price, both the Bank and the judgment-debtors would be benefited by it. Therefore, the learned Judge of the Adalat ought to have allowed the application for transfer of the execution case to a Court of Narayanganj district." 

 38. In the result, the Rules issued in three writ petitions are made absolute. The entire auction process conducted by the Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka in Artha Execution Case No. 204 of 2012 relating to selling the schedule property is hereby set-aside. The Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka is directed to transfer the Execution Case No. 204 of 2012 to the Gazipur District in accordance with law for execution of decree. The Adalat is directed to allow the auction purchaser to withdraw the money deposited against the property.
